grand_strategy.reading: Vanuatu is a small Pacific state that wins where size counts least: at the UN and the ICJ, where its campaign produced the July 2025 advisory opinion and the May 2026 resolution. Its binding limits are money and sovereignty: it needs Chinese and Australian finance, so it bargains over clauses (no foreign base, consultation rather than a veto) instead of aligning, and its coalitions change often enough to stall treaties. Open items: whether the Luganville wharf loan carries a debt-for-equity clause (the sources conflict), the text of the Namele agreement, the status of the Peace Corps programme, and the earthquake recovery after late 2025.

stances.note: Cooperates out of need (aid, policing, seasonal work) and resists alignment: the Nakamal signing was deferred in September 2025 when coalition members feared it would erode sovereignty, then signed on 29 June 2026 with a no-base pledge and consultation, not a veto, over third-party critical infrastructure. No defence treaty exists, so not an ally. Trend warming since the signature and the first official visit by PM Napat. Bond none: the sources show interest, not kinship or sympathy. Grade is our reading of the structure, from the terms of the deal (B).

stances.note: Transactional: a China Eximbank loan for the Luganville wharf, a China-funded presidential palace handed over in July 2024, Chinese police equipment, and the Namele development agreement, still unsigned. Napat calls Namele development cooperation, not a security pact, and says it will be published only after Beijing clears it. Trend warming on the March 2025 envoy visit and the police gift. Friction on record: China said Vanuatu-Australia cooperation should not target any third party, and its embassy denied influencing the Nakamal talks. Bond none: no kinship or sympathy found. The 2023 police vehicles cited by one secondary index are not confirmed by the press piece used, which lists motorbikes and drones.

stances.note: No source uses the word rival: the grade is our reading of the structure (C). The sources show Vanuatu's government opposing France's handling of New Caledonia inside the MSG: its prime minister, Charlot Salwai, who was then MSG chair, said the May 2024 unrest could have been avoided had the French government listened, and the MSG opposed France's constitutional amendment (BenarNews, 15 May 2024). At the MSG leaders' caucus on the sidelines of the 2024 Pacific Islands Forum in Tonga, leaders called for a robust and unified approach to New Caledonia and reiterated support for the FLNKS; the article does not single out Vanuatu as the driver (Islands Business, 2 September 2024). France declared a state of emergency in effect from 16 May 2024 and sent military reinforcements; the source gives no troop figure. Trend cooling is our reading: no source states a trend. Not an adversary: the sources describe a dispute over New Caledonia's status and over how France handled the unrest, with no hostile act between the two states recorded in them. Bond grievance is our reading too: the Kanak independence question is the contested issue; no source calls it a wound between Vanuatu and France.

stances.note: Rival at most, never adversary: Vanuatu seeks Indonesian access and compliance (a UN human-rights visit to West Papua), not Indonesia's end. Friction is escalating: parliament backed West Papua's independence claims in June 2010, Jakarta publicly rebuked Vanuatu at the UN in September 2020, and in September 2026 Vanuatu and Solomon Islands demanded UN access, to which Jakarta replied under right of reply, calling the charges one-sided. No source calls it rivalry, so the grade is our reading (C). Bond grievance: the West Papua dispute itself.

stances.note: Partner on security and money: the US embassy in Port Vila formally opened on 19 July 2024, a decade of Coast Guard ship-rider patrols led by Vanuatu officers, and a commitment of VT185 million to weather forecasting and early warning (July 2026). Peace Corps volunteers have served since 1990 and a return was signalled in 2023-24, but I found no confirmation of their status in 2025-26. Divergence: the United States voted against the May 2026 General Assembly resolution that Vanuatu led to endorse the ICJ opinion, per press summaries. Bond none.

Warming because the treaty is now signed; bond none.

stances_toward.note: Paris holds sovereignty over Matthew and Hunter, the islets Vanuatu claims in its maritime dispute with New Caledonia. The Quai d'Orsay line reported in May 2026 is that the position is unchanged: Paris will not give up sovereignty, though it offers talks on the islets' cultural and customary value. Vanuatu's side has escalated (its government has accused France of colonial practices, in press reports), and Paris answers with its firm position. A territorial claim against French islets is a competing interest, so the posture is rival, not neutral; the one act on record is a French naval landing on the islets, which Port Vila protested, and no use of force is recorded. Cooling is our reading of that escalation. Bond grievance: the claim and the 2024 MSG opposition over New Caledonia. Confidence C: the Quai line reaches us through press reports; the statement itself was not read.
